checks: Extension review shows creator, description, real palette and file icons; starting the appearance package applies its icon set without running its code
Co-Code has its own CoCo icon and control on the right side of the application
Hex edits survive tab and page changes; undo/redo and save preserve an original-byte backup
The binary UI recompiles real C into the selected executable and runs that artifact in a real terminal
Executing locally writes only to the external console; selecting Zénit routes execution exclusively to the main console and retains the animated label
The same three-dot anchor closes its menu; the menu clears the toolbar with a 16px gap
Three menu levels remain separate inside the viewport and extension entries use their display names and package marks
CoCo exposes local, LAN and Internet station modes with the provider notice only for Internet
Copy invitation has breathing room, expands with the shared Forge animation and collapses after click or pointer exit
Zénit and the embedded cross-IDE Monaco client converge after concurrent Unicode edits; a guest saves the shared file on the host
Guests execute in the host environment and receive one shared output stream
A second Zénit joins with virtual buffers, synchronizes and saves on the host without creating fake local files or extension API errors
